title: BullMQ worker: fetching, processing and job locks
intro: Excerpts from the Worker class of BullMQ, a Redis-backed job queue for Node.js, trimmed so they stand alone. A worker pulls jobs from a queue and runs a processor function on each one, several at a time. Redis is replaced by the QueueBackend interface in types.ts; read its comment for what the real backend does. Start with mainLoop in worker.ts.

questions.text: Walk through what happens from mainLoop fetching a job to the job completing.
How does mainLoop limit how many jobs run at once?
What is the LockManager for, and when does it renew locks?
Is there anything in how this worker processes jobs that could cause a job to run more than once? Under what conditions? Point to the lines with a code comment if you can.
Why does processJob call untrackJob in several places, including finally?
Why are DelayedError and WaitingError handled differently from other errors?
How would you make duplicate processing visible in production?
What would you change so a long-running processor is safe?
